sections.html:
Medford is a settled Burlington County township: owners live in 88.2 percent of its homes, and 92.8 percent of residents were in the same house a year earlier. Median home value is $514,800, median household income is $157,969 and median gross rent is $1,589. Population reached about 25,612 in mid-2025, a 4.6 percent gain over 2020.

Owners here tend to stay put, so many houses reach the market after years of one-family use, and the inspection checklist below is worth reading before the first showing. The township covers 38.80 square miles of land, so lots and neighborhoods vary a lot. Route 70 is the main road, joined by County Routes 532, 541 and 544, and most buyers plan on driving. Allow extra time in your plans, because a township this large can mean a long drive between the house, the Fire Department and the county offices.

sections.h2: Pinelands rules that can affect a sale
sections.html:
Medford sits inside the Pinelands National Reserve, and part of the township falls in the state-designated Pinelands Area. The independent borough of Medford Lakes sits entirely inside the township. If your home is in the Pinelands Area, ask the township zoning office what that designation means for additions, tree removal or new outbuildings before a buyer's attorney raises it.

Buyers also recognize local landmarks such as Historic Medford Village, Kirby's Mill, Freedom Park and the Woodford Cedar Run Wildlife Refuge, a 170-acre preserve on the southern border. Nearly 30 glassworkers' homes survive on Trimble Street and Mill Street, and houses near the village carry some historic character that shows up in how they are marketed.

In Medford the Fire Department handles the resale certificate of occupancy, since the construction office inspects existing housing only when someone complains. A house on public water or sewer also needs a visit from the utility billing office for a final meter reading and a sewer inspection, and wells and septic systems fall under the Burlington County Health Department, reached at 609-265-5515 in Westampton.

The fire inspection checks these items:

  • Working smoke detectors on every level, basements included, and within 10 feet of sleeping areas. A system installed with the house and interconnected cannot be swapped for stand-alone battery units.
  • At least one carbon monoxide detector near the bedrooms, with more where bedrooms sit on more than one level.
  • A residential fire extinguisher rated 2A-10BC, no heavier than 10 pounds, mounted no higher than 5 feet and not hidden behind a door or inside a cabinet.

The township asks sellers to leave the detector manuals for the next owner. Contact the Fire Department and the utility office early, since each needs its own visit.

sections.h2: Selling a rental house in Medford
sections.html:
Medford runs an annual inspection program for one- and two-family rentals. Township Council Ordinance 2018-24 requires inspection every year and again at a change of use, ownership or tenancy, so a sale of a rental triggers a new inspection.

Medford rental requirements for one- and two-family houses.
Rental requirementFee or rule
Rental inspection$200 fee, performed by the Construction Code Office
Landlord/tenant registrationFiled with the Township Clerk, $20 application fee
Lead Safe CertificateRequired for rentals built before 1978, from a testing company
Private wellWater test report every 5 years

An investor selling a rental should hand the buyer the latest inspection result, the registration and the lead certificate with the sale documents, so the new landlord can keep the property compliant from the first day.

sections.h2: What a Medford seller owes at closing
sections.html:
The seller owes the state realty transfer fee, which rises with the sale price. Above $1,000,000, a graduated percent fee starting at 1 percent applies to the seller for deeds submitted on or after July 10, 2025.

The Burlington County Clerk records the deed. The recordable-deed checklist calls for the names of seller and buyer, the buyer's address, the price and transfer fee, the seller's residency form (GIT/REP), the municipal block and lot, the seller's notarized signature, the preparer's printed name and a county summary sheet. The recording fee is $45 for the first page, with the summary sheet counting as that page, and $10 for each additional page. A seller claiming a fee exemption also files an Affidavit of Consideration.

The old NJ Transit bus to Philadelphia that ended in Evesham has been discontinued, and Greyhound runs from nearby Mount Laurel. Medford Township Public Schools covers pre-kindergarten through eighth grade, and older students attend Shawnee High School in the Lenape Regional High School District. Burlington County Institute of Technology has a campus in Medford, and St. Mary of the Lakes School is the local Catholic option.

sections.h2: What are the choices for selling a Medford house quickly?
sections.html:
Medford owners can pick a listing agent, a private sale or a cash buyer for a house that needs work, and every route needs the Fire Department certificate and, where applicable, the utility and county health sign-offs.

  • A traditional listing suits a house in good shape and a seller who can wait for a buyer's mortgage and appraisal.
  • A private sale avoids the commission, but the owner then manages disclosures, the contract and the certificate steps without help.
  • A cash sale works for estates, rentals with tenants, houses with septic or well problems, or owners who cannot take on a month of repairs.

Compare offers on the amount left after the mortgage payoff, the transfer fee, and the cost of any repair the inspector requires.

Start the sale by calling the Fire Department to book the resale inspection, and check the detectors and extinguisher yourself first so you do not pay for a second visit. If the house is on public water or sewer, contact the utility billing office for the final meter reading and sewer inspection at the same time. A house with a well or septic system needs the county health department involved before the buyer's attorney asks.

Gather the paperwork the attorney will want: detector manuals, any inspection results, and for a rental the registration and lead certificate. At closing the deed goes to the county clerk with the residency form and the summary sheet. Keep copies of everything in one folder so a delay on one item does not stall the rest. A cash buyer can often close without waiting on a lender's appraisal, but the township and county sign-offs still apply to the house.

faqs.q: Who inspects a Medford house before it sells?
faqs.a: The Medford Fire Department handles the residential resale certificate of occupancy. Homes on public water or sewer also need the utility billing office for a final meter reading and sewer inspection.

faqs.q: What if my Medford house has a well or septic system?
faqs.a: The Burlington County Health Department administers permits and inspections for wells and septic systems. Contact it at 609-265-5515 before listing so any needed work is known early.

faqs.q: Which smoke and carbon monoxide rules does Medford apply?
faqs.a: Smoke detectors are needed on every level, including basements, and within 10 feet of sleeping areas. At least one carbon monoxide detector must be near the bedrooms, and the home needs a 2A-10BC extinguisher of 10 pounds or less.

faqs.q: How is the transfer fee handled on a Medford sale?
faqs.a: The seller pays it at recording, and it grows with the price. Sales above $1,000,000 also pay a graduated percent fee starting at 1 percent.

faqs.q: Do Medford rentals need extra paperwork when sold?
faqs.a: Yes. One- and two-family rentals are inspected annually under Ordinance 2018-24 for $200, registered with the Township Clerk, and need a Lead Safe Certificate if built before 1978. Houses on wells need a water test every 5 years.
